description: The hashed mode of a decision event's arguments (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 8.3): the HMAC-SHA-256, in lowercase hexadecimal, of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785, section 1) of the arguments object as the tool receives it, with a key that the deployment holds. key is that key, in hexadecimal. Each case gives the arguments, their canonical JSON, whose UTF-8 bytes are hashed, and hmac_sha256, the value that the event records with the key's ID. The arguments stay within I-JSON, to which section 1 applies canonical JSON. Strings escape every character beyond printable ASCII, so that invisible ones show. The key is for tests only: it is the SHA-256 of "White Tower conformance test key: hashed-arguments. Never trust it outside tests.", so anyone can compute with it. Never configure it anywhere else.

cases.description: Text beyond ASCII, which RFC 8785 writes as it is, in UTF-8: letters with diacritics, Japanese, a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane (U+1D49C, a surrogate pair in UTF-16) and the line separator U+2028
cases.canonical_json: {"body":"first line second line","greeting":"こんにちは","signature":"𝒜","subject":"Réunion à Göteborg"}

cases.description: The characters that RFC 8785 escapes in a string, a quote, a backslash and the control characters, five of them with their short escapes and the others as \u with four lowercase hexadecimal digits; and those it writes as they are: the solidus, <, >, & and DEL

Nested objects and arrays: the members of every object sorted, at every depth, and the items of every array kept in their order, repeats and empty arrays and objects included; and the largest integer of I-JSON, 2^53 - 1
Members sorted by their UTF-16 code units: B before a, a before aa, aa before b, then U+00E9, then U+1F600 before U+FF61, which their code points, and their UTF-8 bytes, would put the other way
